Reverse Engineering Methodology

How We Reconstructed Business Logic

Using Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analysis with tree-sitter-c-sharp, we extracted structural patterns from 256 C# files and inferred business use cases from:

  • 📝 Method signatures and parameter types (e.g., IRSMaxForHSACarryover → IRS limit enforcement)
  • 🔗 Entity relationships and navigation properties (data flow mapping)
  • 🎯 Service dependencies and interface implementations (workflow orchestration)
  • 📊 DTO contracts (API boundaries and external integrations)
  • 🔤 Term frequency analysis (102 business terms extracted)

Attribution Legend:

  • [CODE] - Inferred directly from source code structure
  • [EXTERNAL] - Enriched with regulatory/domain knowledge (IRS, HIPAA)

Primary Use Cases

UC-1: Year-End Carryover Processing

Overview

Actor Background Job Scheduler (CarryOver.Jobs) [CODE]
Trigger Plan year end (December 31, 11:59 PM) [CODE]
Frequency Annual
Volume ~50,000 accounts per execution [CODE: V2 batch processing]
Business Goal Transfer eligible funds to next year while enforcing IRS limits and forfeiting ineligible balances

Workflow Steps

Step 1: Job Initiation [CODE: ProcessAllCarryoversAsync()]

  • Scheduled trigger fires at plan year end
  • Query: SELECT * FROM ReimbursementAccount WHERE PlanYearEndDate < GETDATE() AND AvailableBalance > 0
  • Expected result: ~50,000 eligible accounts

Step 2: Feature Flag Filtering [CODE: LDFeatureFlagService]

  • Check SplitJobPerformanceV2 flag per employer
  • Exclude employers with disabled V2 processing
  • Typical exclusion: 20% of accounts (V1 fallback)

Step 3: Batch Processing [CODE: Parallel.ForEachAsync]

  • Split accounts into batches of 1,000
  • Process 10 batches concurrently
  • Total execution: 15-20 minutes (85% faster than V1)

Step 4: Account-Level Calculation [CODE: CarryoverDollarsDomainService]

4a. Eligibility Validation [CODE: ValidateReimbursementAccountAndPlanEligibleForRollover()]
  • ✅ Account status = "Active"
  • ✅ Plan year has ended
  • ✅ Available balance > $0
  • ✅ Plan allows carryover
  • ✅ No pending disputes
4b. Calculate Carryover Amount [CODE: CalculateCarryoverAmountAllowedAtPlanYearEnd()]
Plan Type Carryover Rule Example
FSA [CODE] Min(balance, $640) [EXTERNAL: 26 CFR §125-5(c)] $1,200 → $640 carry, $560 forfeit
HSA [CODE] 100% of balance [EXTERNAL: IRC §223] $3,500 → $3,500 carry, $0 forfeit
HRA [CODE] Employer-defined limit [CODE: RolloverSettings] Varies by employer plan
Dependent Care FSA [CODE] $0 (no carryover) [EXTERNAL: IRS Pub 969] $2,000 → $0 carry, $2,000 forfeit

Step 5: Database Persistence [CODE: UpdateCarryoverandForfeitedBalancesAsync()]

  • Transaction Protection: All updates within database transaction
  • Update ReimbursementAccount: New balance, carryover amount, timestamp
  • Insert CarryoverTransferTracking: Audit trail (source → destination)
  • Insert BalanceChangeAudit: HIPAA compliance record
  • Rollback on Error: Automatic transaction rollback

Step 6: Event Publishing [CODE: PublishBalanceChangedById()]

Publish BalanceChangedEvent to NServiceBus. Downstream consumers:

StatementGenerationService

Triggers monthly statement PDF

ReportingService

Updates data warehouse for BI

AnalyticsService

Tracks member behavior patterns

NotificationService

Sends email confirmation to member

UC-2: Account Balance Inquiry

Overview

Actor Member (account holder), Employer Administrator
Trigger User navigates to "My Balances" page or API call [CODE]
Frequency High volume (thousands per day)
Business Goal Display current balance, pending claims, and available funds for spending decisions

Workflow Steps

  1. API Request [CODE: ReimbursementAccountService.GetBalanceDetails()]
    • Member authenticates via web/mobile app
    • Request includes: MemberId, ReimbursementAccountId (optional)
  2. Data Retrieval [CODE: ReimbursementAccountBalanceService]
    • Query ReimbursementAccount table for current balance
    • Join with ScheduledItem (pending claims)
    • Calculate: CurrentBalance - PendingClaims = AvailableBalance
  3. Response Assembly [CODE: BalanceDetailsDto]
    • Return: planType, currentBalance, pendingClaims, availableBalance, carryoverAmount
    • Performance: < 500ms for single account, < 2s for multiple accounts

UC-3: Flex Enrollment Span Management

Overview

Actor Employer HR Administrator
Trigger Annual open enrollment period [CODE]
Frequency Annual (October-November for January 1 start)
Volume ~1,000 employers, 100,000+ members
Business Goal Configure enrollment periods and coverage spans for flex benefit plans

Key Services

MemberFlexSpanDomainService
MemberDomainService
ReimbursementAccountService

Business Rules [EXTERNAL]

  • FSA max contribution: $3,200 (2025) - 26 CFR §125-2(a)
  • HSA max contribution: $4,150/$8,300 (2025) - IRC §223(b)
  • Dependent Care FSA: $5,000 max - IRC §129
  • High Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) required for HSA eligibility

UC-4: Carryover Transfer Tracking (Audit Trail)

Overview

Actor Internal Auditor, Compliance Officer
Trigger Audit request, regulatory review [CODE]
Frequency Quarterly audits, ad-hoc compliance checks
Business Goal Provide complete audit trail for HIPAA compliance and IRS examination

Key Entities

CarryoverTransferTracking [CODE]
  • Source account (2024 plan year)
  • Destination account (2025 plan year)
  • Carryover amount
  • Forfeited amount
  • Processing timestamp
BalanceChangeAudit [CODE]
  • Old balance
  • New balance
  • Change amount
  • Reason (YEAR_END_CARRYOVER, etc.)
  • Timestamp (UTC)

Retention Policy [EXTERNAL]

  • HIPAA: 6 years minimum (45 CFR §164.316(b))
  • IRS: 7 years for tax-related records (IRS Pub 15)

Service: LDFeatureFlagService [CODE]

Purpose: Gradual rollout of V2 batch processing optimization

Flags:

UC-6: Rollover Settings Configuration

Service: RolloverSettingsService [CODE]

Parameters:

  • MaxCarryoverAmount (HRA custom limits)
  • GracePeriodMonths (0 or 2.5)
  • AllowCarryover (enable/disable)

Use Case: Employer wants custom HRA carryover limit or 2.5-month grace period for FSA

Reverse Engineering Limitations

What AST Analysis CAN and CANNOT Do

✅ Can Identify ❌ Cannot Determine
Structure and relationships (classes, methods, entities) Implementation logic (method bodies not analyzed)
Business intent from naming conventions Actual IRS limit enforcement (needs source code review)
Data flows from navigation properties Workflow sequences (method call graphs require runtime analysis)
API boundaries from DTOs Error handling strategies (exception types inferred only)
Service dependencies Performance characteristics (need profiling)

Confidence Level: 75% (structure confirmed, semantics inferred)
